panels.title: Current runtime resource evidence
panels.description: Latest resource-axis evidence at the selected range end, with one row per exporter target and instance UUID. Scores are OIE pressure heuristics (0–100), not utilization percentages. Only fresh, available axes with a recent successful sample and healthy Libvirt/scrape state show a current score; retained or absent axes show Unavailable. Peak is the maximum current axis score. Fresh requires all four axes; Partial / retained means at least one axis remains available. Age is time since the oldest previously successful axis sample, including retained values. Rows require inventory still present in Prometheus; missing inventory is not evidence of a healthy or empty cloud. Open the exporter/source-health panels to investigate unreachable targets.

panels.description: 100 minus the mean idle percentage across logical CPUs, using node_exporter CPU counters over two minutes. Includes I/O wait, IRQ, softirq and steal time as non-idle time. This measures non-idle accounting time; I/O wait does not establish CPU execution saturation.
panels.title: Host CPU Non-Idle Time (Includes I/O Wait)

panels.description:
Actual used memory (Total - Available). Requires Node Exporter.

Source: node_exporter on the hypervisor (kernel-reported host metrics).
Limitations: Host-level view (not per-VM). Memory includes cache/buffers behavior; filesystem usage can differ due to mount options and reserved space; short windows can be noisy if scrapes are delayed.
panels.title: Physical Host RAM Usage

panels.description:
System load average. High load with low CPU usage suggests I/O wait. Requires Node Exporter.

Source: node_exporter on the hypervisor (kernel-reported host metrics).
Limitations: Host-level view (not per-VM). Memory includes cache/buffers behavior; filesystem usage can differ due to mount options and reserved space; short windows can be noisy if scrapes are delayed.
panels.title: Physical Host Load Average (15m)

panels.description:
Used space on the root mount. If this fills up, the hypervisor may crash. Requires Node Exporter.

Source: node_exporter on the hypervisor (kernel-reported host metrics).
Limitations: Host-level view (not per-VM). Memory includes cache/buffers behavior; filesystem usage can differ due to mount options and reserved space; short windows can be noisy if scrapes are delayed.
panels.title: Physical Host Root FileSystem Usage

panels.description: Receive plus transmit drops and errors per second, summed across all interfaces exposed by node_exporter, including physical and virtual interfaces. Uses a generic events-per-second unit. A packet may traverse several virtual interfaces, so these totals are interface events rather than unique affected packets.
panels.title: Host Interface Drops & Errors Rate

panels.description:
Number of times the Linux Kernel killed a process due to Out Of Memory. Should be ZERO.

Source: node_exporter on the hypervisor (kernel-reported host metrics).
Limitations: Host-level view (not per-VM). Memory includes cache/buffers behavior; filesystem usage can differ due to mount options and reserved space; short windows can be noisy if scrapes are delayed.
panels.title: Physical Host OOM Kills (Last 1h)

panels.description:
Hypervisor CPU Commit: active Nova vCPUs divided by host CPU threads. 100% = 1:1 commit; values >100% indicate overcommit.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky.
panels.title: Hypervisor CPU Commit

panels.description:
Total active Nova vCPUs scheduled on each hypervisor.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky.
panels.title: Hypervisor vCPU Allocation

panels.description:
Estimated VM-associated CPU and remaining host CPU, each as a percentage of selected physical CPU threads. VM-associated CPU uses Libvirt domain cpu.time normalized by vCPU count; it includes QEMU virtualization overhead. Remaining host CPU is observed host CPU minus this estimate, clamped at zero. Host CPU excludes idle and I/O wait.

The exporter caps each normalized instance CPU value at 100%, and host/domain observations are not atomic. The split is approximate and cannot isolate guest workload or exact hypervisor overhead. Missing instance CPU measurements produce a gap, not zero workload. The lines are unstacked.
panels.title: Hypervisor CPU Composition (Approximate)

panels.description:
Aggregate host-scheduler runqueue delay across VM vCPUs, in vCPU-seconds per wall-clock second. Libvirt delay/steal is preferred per vCPU and wait is used only as a compatibility fallback; the two aliases are never added.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU vCPU delay and wait counters collected by OIE.
Limitations: Counters can reset on VM reboot or migration; short rate windows can be spiky.
panels.title: Aggregate VM Scheduler Delay

panels.description:
Raw arithmetic difference between selected-host physical RAM and configured instance RAM allocation. Positive values are physical-minus-allocated commit headroom; negative values indicate configured allocation above physical RAM. This is not Nova Scheduler or Placement capacity: it omits allocation ratios, reserved memory, resource-provider inventories and allocations, NUMA or huge-page constraints, and other scheduling policy.

Source: Host physical-memory capacity and Libvirt/OpenStack configured instance allocation collected by OIE.
Limitations: Use Nova Placement and scheduler data for authoritative placement capacity.
panels.title: Physical RAM Minus Instance Allocation (Raw Commit Delta) — range end

panels.description:
Guest-view used-memory estimate across instances divided by each hypervisor's physical RAM capacity. This is a cross-view diagnostic ratio, not the percentage of physical RAM uniquely occupied by VMs.

Source: Libvirt balloon current and usable fields plus host physical-memory capacity collected by OIE.
Limitations: Memory 'used' is derived as balloon current minus balloon usable (the latter corresponds to guest MemAvailable). It is not QEMU RSS or unique physical host RAM consumption and does not include QEMU overhead.

The configured allocation denominator is preserved. Affected aggregates are omitted while any selected visible allocated instance lacks a guest-used measurement or its Libvirt source is unhealthy. Missing memory is not counted as zero. This uses balloon current minus balloon usable; it is not QEMU RSS.
panels.title: Hypervisor Live Instance Memory vs Host Capacity

panels.description:
RAM commit per hypervisor: total instance-allocated RAM divided by host RAM capacity. >100% indicates overcommit.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. RAM allocation is provisioned/configured (scheduler/accounting), not guest 'used'. Clouds may overcommit RAM (e.g., allocation ratios), and this excludes some host overhead.
panels.title: Hypervisor Ram Commit

panels.description:
Total instance-allocated guest RAM (MiB) per hypervisor.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. RAM allocation is provisioned/configured (scheduler/accounting), not guest 'used'. Clouds may overcommit RAM (e.g., allocation ratios), and this excludes some host overhead.
panels.title: Hypervisor Allocated Instance Memory (MiB)

panels.description:
For each hypervisor, the aggregate guest-view used-memory estimate divided by configured memory allocated to those instances.

Source: Libvirt balloon current and usable fields plus configured instance allocation collected by OIE.
Limitations: RAM allocation is provisioned/configured, not guest used. Memory 'used' is derived as balloon current minus balloon usable (the latter corresponds to guest MemAvailable). It is not QEMU RSS or unique physical host RAM consumption and does not include QEMU overhead.

The configured allocation denominator is preserved. Affected aggregates are omitted while any selected visible allocated instance lacks a guest-used measurement or its Libvirt source is unhealthy. Missing memory is not counted as zero. This uses balloon current minus balloon usable; it is not QEMU RSS.
panels.title: Hypervisor Live Instance Ram Use vs Instance Allocation

panels.description:
Total guest-view RAM in use (MiB) by all instances on each hypervisor.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Memory 'used' is a guest-view estimate derived from Libvirt balloon current minus balloon usable (the latter corresponds to guest MemAvailable). It is not QEMU RSS or unique physical host RAM consumption and does not include QEMU overhead.

The configured allocation denominator is preserved. Affected aggregates are omitted while any selected visible allocated instance lacks a guest-used measurement or its Libvirt source is unhealthy. Missing memory is not counted as zero. This uses balloon current minus balloon usable; it is not QEMU RSS.
panels.title: Hypervisor Live Instance Memory (MiB)

panels.description:
Per-hypervisor disk read throughput sourced from instances (guest reads summed at the hypervisor).

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.
panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Read Throughput

panels.description:
Per-hypervisor disk write throughput sourced from instances (guest writes summed at the hypervisor).

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.
panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Write Throughput

panels.description:
Per-hypervisor rolling one-minute disk read volume (GiB) sourced from attached instances. This is not cumulative over the full dashboard time range.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Counter resets or instance migration can affect a short increase window; values do not include backend replication or cluster-internal I/O.
panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Read Volume (Rolling 1 Minute)

panels.description:
Per-hypervisor rolling one-minute disk write volume (GiB) sourced from attached instances. This is not cumulative over the full dashboard time range.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Counter resets or instance migration can affect a short increase window; values do not include backend replication or cluster-internal I/O.
panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Write Volume (Rolling 1 Minute)

panels.description:
Per-hypervisor disk read IOPS (guest read operations summed at the hypervisor).

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.
panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Read IOPS

panels.description:
Per-hypervisor disk write IOPS (guest write operations summed at the hypervisor).

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.
panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Write IOPS

panels.description:
Average disk latency (seconds per operation) aggregated at the hypervisor level for Read, Write, and Flush operations.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.

I/O-weighted calculation: summed service time divided by summed operations. Both sums use the same disks, operation direction, rate window and sample counts; unsupported or currently missing counter pairs are omitted together. This is latency for the observed disk cohort. It excludes unmeasured disks and is not an average of per-disk averages. No operations or unavailable Libvirt telemetry produces a gap; zero latency is not invented.

panels.title: Hypervisor Instance Disk Latency (Avg)

panels.description:
Aggregate Flush IOPS vs Write IOPS at the hypervisor level. High flush rates relative to writes indicate metadata-heavy or sync-heavy workloads.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.

Legacy runtime metrics and utilization totals exclude inactive definitions. XML configuration follows the five-minute metadata cache; state and runtime presence follow the current listing. Metadata is available only while the selected Libvirt source is healthy; deleted/undefined domains are not a Nova inventory. An empty table can mean no matching observations or unavailable telemetry; check the visible coverage indicators.
